paper_title: Stellar cooling bounds on new light particles: plasma mixing effects
suggested_experiment_name: Stellar cooling bounds on B−L vector (Sun, HB stars, cosmological observations)
coupling_convention: g_BL, dimensionless coupling of B−L vector boson
notes: This paper presents updated stellar cooling bounds on multiple coupling types (dark photons, B-L vectors, scalars coupling to electrons/nucleons, Higgs portal scalars) by including plasma mixing effects. However, the paper does NOT present a single unified exclusion plot with extractable numerical (mass, coupling) pairs in a standard format. Instead, it discusses bounds qualitatively and shows several separate figures (Figures 3, 4, 5, 6) for different particle types. The paper states bounds in text form (e.g., 'sin θ ≲ 3×10^-10' for Higgs portal, 'αφ¯ee ≲ 8×10^-31' for electron coupling) but these are mass-dependent and require reading from plots or detailed stellar model calculations. The coupling types discussed include: (1) DarkPhoton (kinetic mixing ε), (2) VectorBL (g_BL coupling), (3) ScalarElectron (φ¯ee coupling, parameterized as α_φee), and (4) ScalarNucleon (φ¯NN coupling). Without access to high-resolution figures or tabulated data, precise numerical extraction is not feasible. The paper emphasizes that their calculations are order-of-magnitude estimates and do not constitute 'robust' constraints, as they use representative stellar models rather than detailed numerical simulations. The main contribution is methodological (including plasma mixing effects) rather than providing a new comprehensive exclusion dataset. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 4 shows constraints on B−L vector coupling g_BL vs mass m_{B-L}. The solid red line represents the main stellar cooling bound from the Sun, which is the lower boundary of the excluded region. The dotted red line shows naive kinetic theory predictions (without plasma mixing effects). The dashed red line indicates bounds neglecting coupling to neutrons. The boundary shows a characteristic minimum around 1–10 MeV, with suppression due to plasma mixing effects at low masses and kinetic-theory behavior at high masses.
